obligations.summary: The AI Office shall encourage and facilitate the drawing up of codes of practice at Union level to contribute to the proper application of this Regulation, taking into account international approaches.

The AI Office and the Board shall aim to ensure that codes of practice cover at least the obligations in Articles 53 and 55, including keeping information up to date, adequate detail on training data summaries, identification of systemic risks, and measures for their assessment and management.

The AI Office may invite all providers of general-purpose AI models and relevant national competent authorities to participate in drawing up codes of practice, with civil society, industry, academia, and other stakeholders able to support the process.

The AI Office and the Board shall aim to ensure that codes of practice clearly set out specific objectives, contain commitments or measures with key performance indicators as appropriate, and take due account of the needs and interests of all interested parties including affected persons.

The AI Office shall aim to ensure that participants in codes of practice report regularly on the implementation of their commitments, measures taken, and outcomes including against key performance indicators, with reporting requirements reflecting differences in size and capacity among participants.
exceptions: Key performance indicators and reporting commitments shall reflect differences in size and capacity between various participants.

obligations.summary: The AI Office and the Board shall regularly monitor and evaluate the achievement of objectives of codes of practice, assess whether they cover obligations in Articles 53 and 55, publish their assessment of adequacy, and the Commission may by implementing act approve a code of practice and give it general validity within the Union.

The AI Office may invite all providers of general-purpose AI models to adhere to codes of practice, with providers not presenting systemic risks permitted to limit adherence to obligations under Article 53 unless they explicitly declare interest in joining the full code.
exceptions: Providers of general-purpose AI models not presenting systemic risks may limit adherence to Article 53 obligations unless they explicitly declare interest to join the full code.

obligations.summary: The AI Office shall encourage and facilitate the review and adaptation of codes of practice, particularly in light of emerging standards, and shall assist in the assessment of available standards.

Codes of practice shall be ready by 2 May 2025, and if not finalised or deemed inadequate by 2 August 2025, the Commission may provide by implementing acts common rules for the implementation of obligations in Articles 53 and 55.
exceptions: If a code of practice cannot be finalised or is deemed inadequate by 2 August 2025, the Commission may substitute it with implementing acts providing common rules.
